result.topic_en: The page completes a fragment reducing a sum of three fourth powers to the form ½ab(a²+b²), notes that 1+z−z³ is a square for z=11/9, and proves the impossibility of the cubic equations z³ = py³ ± p²x³ and az³ ± bpy³ ± cp²x³ = 0 by infinite descent.
result.transcription:
Fragmenta ex Adversariis depromta. 217
Quodsi jam hic restituamus $\alpha ff = a$ et $\beta gg = b$, colligitur $x^4 + y^4 + z^4 = \frac{1}{2}ab(aa+bb)$. Quaeritur ergo num huic aequationi satisfieri possit; tum autem fiet
$n = \frac{1}{2}\alpha\beta, \quad s = 2nfg$ vel $\alpha\beta fg$, et $p = \frac{xx}{fg}, \quad q = \frac{yy}{fg}$ et $r = \frac{zz}{fg}$,
atque hinc porro $A = a - b$ et $E = a + b, \; B = 2x, \; C = 2y$ et $D = 2z$,
verum ne his quidem ambagibus est opus, cum enim fieri debeat $B^4 + C^4 + D^4 = E^4 - A^4$. Statuatur
$A = a - b$ et $E = a + b$, fietque $E^4 - A^4 = 8a^3b + 8ab^3 = 8ab(aa+bb)$,
ergo utrinque per 16 dividendo prodit
$\frac{1}{2}ab(aa+bb) = \frac{B^4 + C^4 + D^4}{16} = x^4 + y^4 + z^4.$
A. m. T. I. p. 281.

51.

Notatu digna est haec formula: $1 + z - z^3$, quae fit quadratum sumto $z = \frac{11}{9}$, qui tamen valor per regulas vulgares non elicitur. Hinc ista quaestio:
Numerum 2 dividere in duas partes $x$ et $2 - x$, quarum productum $2x - xx$ sit numerus formae $z^3 - z$; tum enim erit $1 - 2x + xx = 1 + z - z^3$, ideoque $1 - x = \sqrt{(1 + z - z^3)}$. Sumto ergo $z = \frac{11}{9}$, erit $1 - x = \frac{17}{27}$, hinc $x = \frac{10}{27}$, et altera pars $2 - x = \frac{44}{27}$, quarum productum est
$2x - xx = \frac{440}{27^2}$, at vero $z^3 - z = \frac{1331}{729} - \frac{11}{9} = \frac{440}{27^2}$.
A. m. T. I. p. 295.

52.

Theorema I. Si $p$ denotet numerum primum quemcunque, talis aequatio $z^3 = py^3 \pm ppx^3$ semper est impossibilis.
Demonstratio. Quia enim esse deberet $z^3$ divisibile per $p$, ideoque $z = pA$, unde fieret
$ppA^3 = y^3 \pm px^3$, sive $y^3 = ppA^3 \mp px^3$;
foret igitur etiam $y$ divisibilis per $p$. Sit ergo $y = pB$, unde fieret $ppB^3 = pA^3 \mp x^3$, hinc ergo etiam $x$ divisibile esse debet per $p$; hincque ponatur $x = pC$; unde fiet $ppC^3 = A^3 - pB^3$; foret igitur eodem modo $A = pD$, foretque $ppD^3 = pC^3 + B^3$, tum vero etiam $B$ per $p$ divisibilis esse deberet, porro etiam $C$, $D$, etc. in infinitum. Hoc ergo modo singulae litterae $z$, $y$, $x$ non solum per $p$, sed etiam per $pp$, per $p^3$ atque adeo per $p^\infty$ deberent esse divisibiles; quod cum sit absurdum, veritas theorematis est evicta.
Theorema II. Si numeri $a$, $b$, $c$ fuerint primi ad $p$, ita ut nullus eorum per $p$ sit divisibilis, tum etiam haec aequatio $az^3 \pm bpy^3 \pm cppx^3 = 0$ semper est impossibilis.
Demonstratio. Quia enim $a$ per $p$ non est divisibile, $z$ deberet esse divisibile, tum vero etiam pari modo $y$ et $x$, sicque ad eandem aequationem perveniretur, unde patet impossibilitas, uti casu praecedente.
Corollarium. Eadem demonstratio quoque habet locum, si $p$ fuerit productum ex duobus vel pluribus numeris primis diversis, veluti si sit $p = 2.3$, vel $3.5$, vel $3.5.7$, etc.
L. Euleri Op. posthuma. T. I. 28

methods.what: Reduction of B^4+C^4+D^4 = E^4 - A^4 with A=a-b, E=a+b to x^4+y^4+z^4 = ½ab(a²+b²)
Dividing by 16 gives the sum of three fourth powers equal to ½ab(a²+b²)
1+z−z³ is a rational square at z=11/9
methods.quote: Notatu digna est haec formula: $1 + z - z^3$, quae fit quadratum sumto $z = \frac{11}{9}$

methods.what: Splitting 2 into parts whose product has the form z³−z, via (1−x)² = 1+z−z³; numerical check with x=10/27
Infinite descent proof that z³ = py³ ± p²x³ has no nontrivial solutions for prime p
methods.quote: Hoc ergo modo singulae litterae $z$, $y$, $x$ non solum per $p$, sed etiam per $pp$, per $p^3$ atque adeo per $p^\infty$ deberent esse divisibiles

methods.what: Generalisation: az³ ± bpy³ ± cp²x³ = 0 is impossible when a, b, c are prime to p
methods.quote: haec aequatio $az^3 \pm bpy^3 \pm cppx^3 = 0$ semper est impossibilis

methods.what: Extension of the result to squarefree composite p

items.quote: Quaeritur ergo num huic aequationi satisfieri possit
items.english: It is therefore asked whether this equation can be satisfied.

items.quote: qui tamen valor per regulas vulgares non elicitur
items.english: This value, however, is not obtained by the usual rules.

items.quote: Numerum 2 dividere in duas partes $x$ et $2 - x$, quarum productum $2x - xx$ sit numerus formae $z^3 - z$
items.english: To divide the number 2 into two parts x and 2−x whose product 2x−x² is a number of the form z³−z.

items.quote: Si $p$ denotet numerum primum quemcunque, talis aequatio $z^3 = py^3 \pm ppx^3$ semper est impossibilis.
items.english: If p denotes any prime number, such an equation z³ = py³ ± p²x³ is always impossible.

items.quote: Si numeri $a$, $b$, $c$ fuerint primi ad $p$, ita ut nullus eorum per $p$ sit divisibilis, tum etiam haec aequatio $az^3 \pm bpy^3 \pm cppx^3 = 0$ semper est impossibilis.
items.english: If the numbers a, b, c are prime to p, so that none of them is divisible by p, then the equation az³ ± bpy³ ± cp²x³ = 0 is also always impossible.

items.quote: Eadem demonstratio quoque habet locum, si $p$ fuerit productum ex duobus vel pluribus numeris primis diversis, veluti si sit $p = 2.3$, vel $3.5$, vel $3.5.7$, etc.
items.english: The same demonstration also holds if p is a product of two or more distinct primes, for example p = 2·3, or 3·5, or 3·5·7, etc.
